chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, from Ibn Mahboub, from Jameel ibn Darraj, who said:

I said to Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him), 'Sometimes I remember these weak ones (of understanding), so I say that we and they are in the dwellings of Paradise.' So Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) said, 'Allah would not do that with you all, ever!'
ai.seo_question: Do the weak and the knowledgeable share the same level in Paradise?
ai.summary: In this hadith from *Al-Kafi*, Imam al-Sadiq (AS) corrects the narrator’s assumption that the 'weak ones' (al-mustad'afin) share an identical spiritual rank with the knowledgeable, emphasizing that Paradise is stratified according to one's degree of understanding and faith. This distinction highlights the Shia scholarly principle that intellectual and spiritual depth directly influence one's station in the hereafter, rather than mere inclusion in the community of believers. The Imam’s emphatic denial ('God will never do that to you') underscores the importance of not equating the righteous with those of lesser spiritual capacity.
